piece_type: DTC branded website (landing page and 'Responses' webpage)
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.claim: “Most people achieved a response with Niktimvo” | “75% of people (59 out of 79) experienced a response”
cases.context: PI: no complete responses; all 59 responders were partial responses; CR/PR definitions shown but do not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Implies complete responses when 0% CR was observed.
cases.check: Do response-rate claims disclose response type (e.g., all partial) when unqualified 'response' could imply complete response?

cases.claim: “Niktimvo may offer fast and lasting responses” | “In a study of people experiencing chronic GVHD symptoms after taking at least 2 therapies, Niktimvo™ (axatilimab-csfr) delivered fast and lasting responses” | “Niktimvo provided lasting responses o More than half (60%) of the people who showed a response to Niktimvo continued to respond for at least 1 year” (next to a flipping calendar image)
cases.context: PI: median time to response 1.5 months (range 0.9-5.1); median duration of response 1.9 months; 60% measure excludes progression.
cases.rationale: 'Fast' and 'lasting' overstate onset and durability; alternative durability metric conflates measures.
cases.check: Rule: flag 'fast'/'rapid'/'lasting'/'durable' descriptors and require them to be checked against label median time-to-response and duration-of-response.

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (organ-level responses)
cases.claim: “People achieved responses in multiple affected organs” | “Niktimvo may provide fast and lasting responses across a range of affected organs” with a body diagram of organ-specific response rates
cases.context: Efficacy based on ORR across all organs, not individual organs.
cases.rationale: Organ-level response rates inflate perceived benefit and ignore progression in other organs.
cases.check: Does the piece present subcomponent/organ-level results that were not the basis of approval as standalone efficacy?

cases.claim: “Niktimvo offered symptom improvement” | “44 out of 79 people who received Niktimvo (56%) reported improvement in the specific chronic GVHD symptoms assessed in the study.” | “Symptom improvement was defined as a reduction in chronic GVHD symptoms compared to the start of the study.”
cases.context: PI: exploratory analysis of modified Lee Symptom Scale (symptom bother), not number of symptoms.
cases.rationale: Mischaracterizes an exploratory symptom-bother measure as reduction in symptoms.
cases.check: Does the description of a PRO endpoint match what the instrument actually measures, and is its exploratory status respected?
